modmenu.descriptionTranslation.livinghor: Gives life to the distance: animals, villagers and other players stay visible far past your render distance, players who logged off live on where they left, and birds fill the sky. Works with the game alone or on top of Voxy and Distant Horizons.
livinghorizon.options.title: Living Horizon
livinghorizon.options.preset.tooltip: Sets the settings below to reasonable values for the desired quality: how many distant entities are shown, and how far. High and Ultra are for powerful computers. Changing a setting by hand switches to Custom.
livinghorizon.options.preset.name: Preset
livinghorizon.options.enabled.tooltip: Keeps showing other players past the distance where the server stops sending them. The "Toggle Distant Players" key switches this too.
livinghorizon.options.showVehicles.toolt: Shows what a distant player is riding: horse, boat, minecart, happy ghast...
livinghorizon.options.offlinePlayers.too: Players who logged off stay where they were until they come back. OFF: they are neither shown nor remembered.
How many players who logged off are shown at once, nearest first. The others stay remembered, and show again once among the nearest. Lowering it improves performance.
livinghorizon.options.offlineLife.toolti: Players who logged off go about their day: they stroll, sit, use chests and workstations, sleep in a bed at night and raise a shield against monsters. OFF: they sit where they logged off.
livinghorizon.options.offlineRoam.toolti: How far from where they logged off offline players walk around and look for a bed, a chest or a workstation. 50 blocks is about a village.
livinghorizon.options.offlineNames.toolt: Shows an offline player's name above them, marked (offline). Looking at them up close shows when they were last seen.
livinghorizon.offline.test.spawned: Test player %s placed where you stand, logged off. Step back to see them; /livinghorizon debug offline test clear removes them.
livinghorizon.offline.test.spawnedMany: %s test players placed within %s blocks of you, logged off. /livinghorizon debug offline test clear removes them.
livinghorizon.offline.test.switchedOff: Logged-off players are switched off in the settings: turn them on to see %s.
livinghorizon.offline.test.long: %s is too long: a player name has 16 characters at most.
livinghorizon.offline.test.none: Nobody who logged off is remembered on this server.
livinghorizon.options.renderTrackedVehic: The game hides small entities like boats early, so a player in a boat would float on nothing. Keeps a vehicle shown while a player rides it.
livinghorizon.options.distantMobs.toolti: Animals, villagers and golems stay visible once out of range, where they were, wandering, looking around and grazing.
livinghorizon.options.maxDistantMobs.too: How many distant mobs are shown at once, nearest first. Lowering it improves performance. Warning: Unlimited here and in Mob Render Distance can crash the game.
livinghorizon.options.distantEntities.to: Boats, vehicles and mannequins stay visible once out of range, where they were left.
livinghorizon.options.maxDistantEntities: How many distant boats, vehicles and mannequins are shown at once, nearest first, apart from Max Mobs. Lowering it improves performance.
livinghorizon.options.mobMaxDistance.too: How far away distant mobs are shown. Unlimited: as far as they are remembered. Warning: Unlimited here and in Max Mobs can crash the game.
How far away distant boats, vehicles and mannequins are shown, apart from mobs. Unlimited: as far as they are remembered.
livinghorizon.options.animationMinPixels: Mobs smaller than this on screen stop their walking and idle animations, which could not be seen anyway. Lower is livelier; higher improves performance.
livinghorizon.options.animationMaxDistan: Past this distance, distant mobs are no longer animated, however big they look. For less powerful computers.
How far away distant players are shown.
livinghorizon.options.depthOcclusion.too: Distant entities hide behind Voxy or Distant Horizons terrain, even half behind a tree. Needed with Distant Horizons, and with shader packs like Photon.
livinghorizon.options.extendFarPlane.too: The game stops drawing at four times the render distance. ON: very distant players are still drawn where they are. OFF: they are drawn closer and smaller, and can show through terrain.
Distant entities are never drawn smaller than this, so they are easier to spot. OFF: true size.
livinghorizon.status.none: No other player is being followed.
livinghorizon.status.pack.on: Shared positions: running (the server or the LAN host has the mod), positions are exact.
livinghorizon.status.pack.off: Shared positions: not found (the server or the LAN host does not have the mod), distant players are not shown.
livinghorizon.sharing.none: Living Horizon: this server does not have the mod, so distant players are not shown.
livinghorizon.sharing.updateGame: Living Horizon: the server has a newer version of the mod, so distant players are not shown until the mod in this game is updated.
livinghorizon.sharing.updateServer: Living Horizon: the server has an older version of the mod, so distant players are not shown until the server's mod is updated.
livinghorizon.status.cost: Cost: %s ms per tick, %s ms per frame; %s puppets drawn, %s skipped (behind you or too small).
livinghorizon.lod.missing: Neither Voxy nor Distant Horizons is installed: nothing to hide behind.
livinghorizon.lod.depth: Far terrain depth on distant mobs: %s.
livinghorizon.lod.probe.hit: Looking ahead, the first block %s knows is %s blocks away.
livinghorizon.lod.probe.none: Looking ahead, %s knows no block within 4096 blocks.
A mob with a name tag is always remembered and shown, whatever its type.
livinghorizon.options.seedMobs.tooltip: Shows the animals the world puts in land nobody has explored yet, about where you will find them. Needs the mod on the server; always there in single player.
livinghorizon.options.onlyOverTerrain.to: Distant mobs are only drawn where terrain is drawn under them: the game's own, or Voxy or Distant Horizons terrain. Off, a mob remembered where nothing is drawn yet floats in the void.
livinghorizon.options.chooseMobs.tooltip: Choose one by one which mobs, boats and other entities stay visible far away.
livinghorizon.options.forgetMobs.tooltip: Forgets every mob, boat and vehicle remembered on this server. Those a server with the mod shares come back by themselves; the others once met again.
livinghorizon.options.forgetMobs.confirm: Every mob, boat and vehicle remembered on this server is forgotten. Those a server with the mod shares come back by themselves; the others once met again.
livinghorizon.options.scanMobs.tooltip: Finds the mobs in the chunks around right away, without going there: they appear on the horizon at once. Mobs no longer found are forgotten.
livinghorizon.options.scanMobs.unavailab: Single player only: a server never sends mobs far away. On a server with the mod, the server shares them.
livinghorizon.options.scanRadius.tooltip: How far around a scan looks, in chunks. A scan of this size runs by itself on first entering a single player world. Also /livinghorizon scan <distance>.
livinghorizon.options.foreseeMobs.toolti: Works out from the seed the animals the world puts in the land nobody has explored around you, as far as the radius beside, and shows them on the horizon. A large radius takes a few minutes.
livinghorizon.options.foreseeMobs.unavai: Only in single player, or on a server with the mod that shares its seed.
livinghorizon.options.foreseeRadius.tool: How far around Guess Nearby Mobs looks, in chunks, up to 1024. Also /livinghorizon foresee <distance>.
livinghorizon.scan.started: Reading the mobs of the chunks within %s chunks...
livinghorizon.scan.done: Scan done: %s mobs found within %s chunks.
livinghorizon.scan.failed: The scan failed: see the log.
livinghorizon.scan.unavailable: Scanning only works in a single player world: a server never sends the mobs of chunks far from you. On a server with the mod, the server shares them.
livinghorizon.foresee.started: Guessing the animals of the land nobody explored within %s chunks...
livinghorizon.foresee.failed: The guess failed: see the log.
livinghorizon.foresee.unavailable: Guessing only works in single player, or on a server with the mod that shares its seed.
livinghorizon.foresee.off: Unexplored Land Mobs is off in the settings.
livinghorizon.benchmark.started: Living Horizon benchmark: about %s seconds. Stand still, look at what you play with, and touch nothing until the report is written. /livinghorizon benchmark stop to stop it.
livinghorizon.benchmark.running: A benchmark is already running. /livinghorizon benchmark stop to stop it.
livinghorizon.benchmark.failed: Benchmark done, but the report could not be written: %s
livinghorizon.benchmark.stopped: Benchmark stopped. Your settings are back as they were.
livinghorizon.benchmark.aborted: Benchmark stopped: the world closed or the game was paused. Your settings are back as they were.
livinghorizon.benchmark.phase.mobs-no-oc: distant mobs, Skip Hidden Mobs off
livinghorizon.benchmark.phase.mobs-no-fa: distant mobs, Hide Behind Far Terrain off
livinghorizon.benchmark.world.explain: This makes a NEW world, "Living Horizon benchmark", added to your world list: the world you are in is saved and closed, never changed or replaced (on a server, you leave it). The new world is always the same: a flat world with every mob placed by the mod, nothing random. Building it takes a minute or two. Type /livinghorizon benchmark world confirm to go ahead.
livinghorizon.benchmark.world.name: Living Horizon benchmark
livinghorizon.benchmark.world.building: Building the benchmark world: generating the land around, placing the mobs. Do not move until it says it is ready.
livinghorizon.benchmark.world.ready: The benchmark world is ready. Type /livinghorizon benchmark: in this world it always runs from the same spot and view, so its reports compare from one version of the mod to the next.
livinghorizon.benchmark.world.failed: The benchmark world could not be made: %s
livinghorizon.options.restoreDefaults.to: Puts every setting of this screen back to its default, the chosen mobs and birds included.
livinghorizon.options.restoreDefaults.co: Every Living Horizon setting goes back to its default, including the mobs and birds you chose. Remembered mobs are kept.
livinghorizon.options.forgetSleepers.too: Removes every offline player shown on this server. On a server with the mod, they come back at their last position.
livinghorizon.options.forgetSleepers.con: Every offline player shown on this server disappears. On a server with the mod, they come back at their last position.
livinghorizon.options.mobTypes.title: Distant Mobs & Entities
livinghorizon.options.mobTypes.tab.entit: Boats, vehicles and the other entities that are not mobs. A minecart or another mod's vehicle appears here once you have seen one.
livinghorizon.options.mobTypes.shared.to: %s - ★ shared by a server with the mod: shown even if never met. Roaming: walks around. Still: stays where it was.
livinghorizon.options.mobTypes.local.too: %s - not shared by the server: shown only where it was met. Roaming: walks around. Still: stays where it was.
livinghorizon.options.mobTypes.vehicle.s: %s - ★ shared by a server with the mod: shown even if never met. Stays where it was left.
livinghorizon.options.mobTypes.vehicle.l: %s - not shared by the server: shown only where it was met. Stays where it was left.
livinghorizon.options.skyBirds.tooltip: Birds and bats all around: flocks, geese, birds of prey, seagulls, pigeons, robins, tits, ducks, bats at night. Nobody else sees them.
livinghorizon.options.birdMaxDistance.to: How far away birds can fly. Far ones are only a few pixels, like real birds.
livinghorizon.options.birdDensity.toolti: How many birds, all kinds together. 100% is normal, 200% twice as many.
livinghorizon.options.birdMinHeight.tool: Flocks and birds of prey never fly lower than this above the player, or above the sea if higher.
livinghorizon.options.chooseBirds.toolti: Choose which kinds of birds appear.
livinghorizon.options.birdTypes.title: Bird Types
livinghorizon.options.birdTypes.flocks.t: Clouds of small birds crossing the sky, far away.
livinghorizon.options.birdTypes.geese.to: Large birds flying high in a V.
Large birds circling a spot, gliding, drifting with the wind.
livinghorizon.options.birdTypes.gulls.to: White birds low over beaches and the sea; now and then one lands on the beach, and takes off if you come close.
Sitting on the top of tall buildings; they take off when you come close and land again later.
livinghorizon.options.birdTypes.robins.t: Hopping and pecking in fields of crops; they fly off when you come close.
livinghorizon.options.birdTypes.tits.too: Flitting about the tops of trees.
livinghorizon.options.birdTypes.ducks.to: On lakes, rivers and ponds; now and then they fly to another spot. They never let you come near.
livinghorizon.options.birdTypes.bats.too: At night, flitting around the scenery, or hanging upside down under leaves and roofs near you until you come close. They go home at dawn.
Now and then a flock of the game's parrots.
livinghorizon.options.easterEggs.tooltip: A few surprises, now and then. Nobody else sees them.
livinghorizon.ee.nothing: Nothing comes. Not here, not now.
livinghorizon.bird.off: Birds are off here: switch them on in the settings, in the Overworld.
livinghorizon.bird.hidden: %s are switched off: turn them on in Bird Types... in the settings.
livinghorizon.bird.no_place: No place around for %s: look at a tree, water, a field, a tall building or the coast, or go nearer one.
livinghorizon.options.birdSize.tooltip: Draws birds bigger than life, to see them better. 1x is real size.
livinghorizon.options.birdStyle.tooltip: 3D: small models with flapping wings, like the game's mobs. 2D: flat pixel drawings, lighter. Bats and parrots are the game's own either way.
livinghorizon.options.hideOccludedMobs.t: Distant mobs the terrain hides entirely (the far terrain included) are not drawn at all, instead of drawn and covered pixel by pixel. Cheaper with many mobs. Decided from the depth of the picture: a mob even partly in view is still drawn, and one shows up a frame or two after the view clears.
livinghorizon.options.impostors.tooltip: Past a distance, mobs are drawn as flat pictures instead of full 3D models. The difference is hard to see from afar, and performance is much better with many mobs.
livinghorizon.options.impostorEntities.t: Boats, vehicles and mannequins are simplified too, like mobs. OFF: they keep their full model at any distance.
livinghorizon.options.impostorDistance.t: Distance from which entities are simplified. Lower improves performance; higher keeps full models longer.
livinghorizon.options.impostorPixels.too: Entities smaller than this on screen are simplified too, even closer than the Simplification Distance. Higher improves performance; OFF uses the distance alone.
livinghorizon.options.debug.tooltip: Tools to see what the mod does, and settings for Distant Horizons, Voxy and shader packs. Best left as they are unless something looks wrong.
livinghorizon.options.debug.title: Debug Options
livinghorizon.options.discord.tooltip: Opens the mod's Discord server, to ask a question or report a problem.
livinghorizon.options.changelog.tooltip: Shows what changed in each version of the mod.
livinghorizon.changelog.title: Changelog
livinghorizon.options.impostorPreview.to: Shows the pictures used for simplified entities, and rebuilds them if one looks wrong.
livinghorizon.options.impostorPlayers.to: Distant players are simplified too, like mobs. OFF: they keep their full model at any distance, so their skin and armor stay in full detail.
Video memory the pictures of simplified mobs may take, apart from the players'. Taken only as new looks are met; when it is full, the picture unused for longest makes room.
livinghorizon.options.impostorPlayerMemo: Video memory the pictures of simplified players may take, riders and what they ride included, apart from the mobs'. A picture unused for a minute is thrown away.
livinghorizon.options.debugHud.tooltip: Top left. In the F3 screen, turn on "living_horizon" in the debug options (F3 + F6): cost per tick and frame, what became of every distant mob in the last frame, far terrain reads and depth, how far this server sends mobs, which optimisations are on.
livinghorizon.options.debugBoxes.tooltip: A box and a dot around every distant mob and player, seen through terrain, in the colour of what became of it: green copy drawn, cyan real mob drawn by the mod, blue player, yellow too small, orange behind blocks, red outside the view, purple being built, grey past the maximum. Pink: an animal foreseen from the seed.
livinghorizon.options.debugLabels.toolti: Over each box: what became of it, its kind, its distance and its size on screen in pixels.
livinghorizon.options.debugGameMobs.tool: White boxes around the mobs the game draws itself, to see where the mod takes over.
livinghorizon.options.outlines.open.tool: An outline seen through terrain around each kind of figure, in the colours of the boxes, each on its own switch: to compare screenshots with and without an optimisation.
livinghorizon.options.boxes.open.tooltip: A box seen through terrain around each distant figure, and its label, each kind on its own switch, in the colours of the outlines.
livinghorizon.options.boxLiveMobs.toolti: Cyan: the real mobs the server sends that the mod draws.
livinghorizon.options.boxCopies.tooltip: Green: the copies of mobs met, which the server no longer sends.
livinghorizon.options.boxForeseen.toolti: Pink: the animals foreseen from the seed in land nobody explored, never seen.
livinghorizon.options.boxLeftOut.tooltip: The mobs left out of the frame, in the colour of why: too small, behind blocks, over the void, outside the view...
livinghorizon.options.outlineGameMobs.to: White: the mobs and players the game draws itself, near you.
livinghorizon.options.outlineLiveMobs.to: Cyan: real mobs the server still sends, drawn by the mod past the game's entity distance.
livinghorizon.options.outlineCopies.tool: Green: the full models the mod draws for mobs the server no longer sends, and its birds.
livinghorizon.options.outlineForeseen.to: Pink: the copies of animals foreseen from the seed in land nobody explored, never seen.
livinghorizon.options.outlinePlayers.too: Blue: the distant players the mod draws, online or logged off.
livinghorizon.options.outlineImpostors.t: Magenta: the flat pictures drawn instead of a model, for a mob or a player.
livinghorizon.options.outlineLeftOut.too: A cross where a distant mob is not drawn at all, in the colour of why: yellow too small, orange behind blocks, red outside the view, purple being built, grey past the maximum. Only where it is, not what it is.
livinghorizon.options.debugDepthView.too: The depth buffer in the bottom right corner, near white to far black, the sky in blue.
livinghorizon.options.optViewCulling.too: Copies behind you or to the side are not prepared at all.
livinghorizon.options.optTinyCulling.too: Copies smaller than about half a pixel are not prepared (only at true size, Minimum Size OFF).
livinghorizon.options.optLazyDepth.toolt: The far terrain's depth (Voxy or Distant Horizons) is merged only on frames that draw something past the render distance. Off: every frame.
livinghorizon.options.optParallelRead.to: The far world (Voxy or Distant Horizons) is read on several threads at once. Off: one thread.
livinghorizon.options.optColumnCache.too: Ground already read in the far world is kept two minutes. Off: read again every time.
livinghorizon.options.optOcclusionQuerie: How "Skip Hidden Mobs" decides, which must be ON: the GPU tests each mob's box against the depth of the picture - what you see, Voxy or Distant Horizons included - and a mob with not one pixel in view is not drawn. OFF, to compare: lines of sight are traced in the far terrain's world instead, which needs Voxy or Distant Horizons.
livinghorizon.options.optDhFade.tooltip: Without a shader pack, Distant Horizons fades the game's picture into its terrain past the render distance, which would paint over the distant mobs: they are kept out of that fade. Off, to compare.
livinghorizon.options.optVoxyShadows.too: With Voxy and a shader pack like Photon, terrain behind a distant mob can wrongly cast its shadow on it. ON: fixed. OFF: Voxy is left untouched and those shadows show.
livinghorizon.options.optVoxyFog.tooltip: Without a shader pack, distant mobs past a certain distance turn paler than Voxy's terrain around them. ON: they get the same fog as that terrain; enchantment glints and lightning fade a little sooner. OFF: the game's fog.
livinghorizon.options.optFreezeHidden.to: A distant mob that is not drawn (out of view, behind terrain, too small) stops moving: it is only a position until it shows again. Saves their animation and path reads. Off by default, to compare.
livinghorizon.options.optStillTiny.toolt: A distant mob only a few pixels high on screen slides and turns without playing its walking and idle animations, which could not be seen. Off: always animated.
livinghorizon.options.optBackgroundBuild: Saved mobs are read off the game's thread and built within 2 ms per tick. Off: all at once, on the game's thread.
livinghorizon.debug.on: Living Horizon debug: on (panel and boxes).
livinghorizon.debug.hud.title: Living Horizon - debug
livinghorizon.debug.hud.mobs: Mobs: %s remembered, %s chosen, %s built, %s waiting, %s sent by the server
livinghorizon.debug.hud.depth: Far terrain depth: %s; merged last frame: %s
livinghorizon.debug.hud.reads: Far terrain reads: %s threads, %s tasks pending, %s columns known
livinghorizon.debug.f3.polygons: Living Horizon: %s polygons (%s triangles) - %s full models, %s polygons; %s impostors
livinghorizon.debug.f3.impostors: Living Horizon impostors: %s sheets baked, %s waiting
livinghorizon.debug.f3.impostorsFailed: Living Horizon impostors: baking failed, full models are used (see the log)
livinghorizon.impostors.title: Picture Preview
livinghorizon.impostors.off: Simplified Mobs, Entities and Players are all OFF: turn one on in the settings to make and use the pictures.
livinghorizon.impostors.empty: No pictures yet: those of the distant players and mobs around are made within a few seconds.
livinghorizon.impostors.regenerate.toolt: Throws every picture away and makes them again, even after a failure.
livinghorizon.debug.hud.profile: Cost per section (last, average, worst of 5 s)
livinghorizon.debug.opt.lazy: far terrain depth only when needed
livinghorizon.debug.opt.fade: mobs kept out of DH's fade
livinghorizon.debug.opt.shadows: mobs in Voxy's depth for shadows
